title: The harp that once did starve us all.
html_source: Thorton: “ Bloom is parodying the opening line of Thomas Moore’s "The Harp That Once through Tara’s Halls,” which begins “The harp that once through Tara’s halls/ The soul of music shed,/ Now hangs as mute on Tara’s walls,/ As if that soul were fled.”

anchor.text: The harp that once did starve us all.
anchor.prefix: ink against their breath. More power, Pat. Coarse red: fun for drunkards: guffaw and smoke. Take off that white hat. His parboiled eyes. Where is he now? 1961#167Beggar somewhere.
anchor.suffix: I was happier then. Or was that I? Or am I now I? Twentyeight I was. She twentythree. When we left Lombard street west something changed. Could never like it again after Rudy.
